ideas.description: Lengthen the 28 px middle stage on the E048 tip. The tip is commit dc07126: bs 1536; 20 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5, 28 px for 1.5-3.0, 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs, 6.75 total; SGD-group lr x1.5; head lr x2 with wd halved; Muon lr 0.16, mom 0.8, NS3; lookahead 0.97^5; brightness/contrast jitter; whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. If I066 (head x3) is kept first, use its commit instead. Make one change: move the 28 -> 32 px switch from 3.0 to 3.5 epochs, so 28 px runs for 2.0 epochs and 32 px for the last 3.25. Total epochs, bs, the sample stream and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged. The switch now falls mid-epoch (sample 175000, inside a bs-1536 step). Train the first part of that epoch's permutation at 28 px and the rest at 32 px, splitting the straddling step into the two partial shapes, as the existing switches do. In build(), warm up every new partial-batch shape at the 3.5-epoch switch for the 28 px and 32 px graphs (no whitening-bias grad), using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Keep build under ~450 s. Run debug_nan.py on any new shape and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times. Rationale: E048 showed that 1.5 epochs at 28 px cost ~0.0-0.2 pp for -5.2%, an exchange rate of ~0.05 pp per 1%, cheaper than any other lever left. E043 warned that low-fidelity steps cost more past the lr peak, but 28 px keeps far more detail than 24 px. This run prices the next half-epoch.
ideas.expected: Time -1.0% to -3.0%, point -1.9% (~4.905 s vs 5.000 s): 0.5 epoch moves from ~0.82 s to ~0.64 s per epoch at bs 1536. Accuracy -0.40 to +0.20 pp, point -0.12 pp (~0.7540). Feasible means a new best with a ~0.1 pp margin. A drop >=0.3 pp means 28 px steps are no longer cheap past ~3 epochs: fix the switch at 3.0 and close stage-length tuning. If it lands at 0.751-0.753, keep the code and pair it with the next accuracy gain (I066/I064/new aug idea).

ideas.description: Weaker augmentation only in the low-resolution stages, following D014 C0193: small images want weaker augmentation, as in EfficientNetV2's progressive learning. This replaces the all-stage translate removal, I063. On the tip (E048, or I066's successor if it is kept), make one change: turn off translate-2 during the 20 px and 28 px stages (epochs 0-3.0) and keep it in the 32 px stage. The alternating flip and brightness/contrast jitter stay in every stage. Translate is pad-and-random-crop inside the compiled augment, so use a separate augment variant for the low-res stages and pick it in Python by stage. Never put a data-dependent branch in the graph. Tensor shapes are unchanged. Warm up the new augment variant in build() with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. The RNG stream for flips and jitter should stay as is where possible; note in the run log whether the translate draws are skipped, since skipping them shifts the downstream RNG. Eval is unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.30 to +0.35 pp, point +0.05 pp; time -0.1% to -0.5%, since the low-res augment is cheaper. A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.8.2 in its low-res form and banks margin for I067 (16 px), bs 2048 (I057) or the longer 28 px stage. A drop >=0.25 pp means translate still helps early even at low res. Then close the augmentation-strength axis, and I063's all-stage removal is moot.

ideas.description: Cut one Newton-Schulz iteration using Turbo-Muon's AOL preconditioning (arxiv 2512.04632). Gate it first in drafts/, untimed: with drafts/time_muon.py on the tip's batched compiled Muon step, measure the GPU time of NS3 against NS2+AOL. Launch only if the saving is >=0.3 ms/step. At ~221 steps that is ~0.07 s, about 1.3%, which is near jitter, so a smaller saving cannot be graded. If the gate passes, make one change on the tip (E048 or its successor). Inside the batched compiled Muon step, after the existing pre-NS normalization, compute the first Gram matrix A = X^T X (or X X^T on the short side, as the existing NS uses). Rescale X by diag(rowsum|A|)^-1/2 on that side, rescale A to match so it is reused rather than recomputed, then run 2 quintic iterations instead of 3 with the same coefficients. The sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling, weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead and everything else stay unchanged. In drafts/, also log the max singular value of the NS output for each shape group on a few real momentum matrices. Compare NS3 against NS2+AOL to confirm that orthogonalization quality matches. Run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. Warm up in build() on synthetic tensors.
ideas.expected: If the gate passes: Muon GPU time -0.3 to -0.45 ms/step, mean time -1.2% to -2.0%, point -1.5% (~4.92 s). Accuracy within +-0.2 pp, point -0.03 pp: E017 showed NS5 -> NS3 cost nothing. A time gain >=1.2% with accuracy >=0.753 supports H2.4.5 and is kept. A drop >=0.25 pp means NS2 under-orthogonalizes the 128x1152 group; the follow-up is NS2 only on the 384/576 groups. If the gate fails, mark H2.4.5 refuted without a run: NS bmm is not where the remaining Muon time goes.

drop.reason: Its point estimate (+0.07 pp) is below re-draw noise. The averaging axis is flat: horizon E028, BN recal E035, tail floor E033. The lookahead schedule is unlikely to be where the margin comes from. The low-res augmentation and head/BN-bias ideas get the accuracy-gain slots instead.

Replaced by the low-res-only translate removal. Removing translate in the 32 px stage carries the larger downside (point -0.15 pp at a 0.22 pp margin). D014 C0193 supports weakening augmentation only at small image sizes, so that version tests H1.8.2 with a better expected value.

The cheapest time cuts left price accuracy at ~0.05-0.08 pp per 1% of time: the low-res stages, bs 1536 to 2048, and a 16 px first stage. Cutting epochs costs ≥0.12 pp per 1%, so it is a worse trade. The queue therefore alternates small time cuts with accuracy-margin builders.

- **No translate in the low-res stages only (H1.8.2, priority 3).** Backed by D014 C0193; replaces I063.
- **NS2 with AOL preconditioning (H2.4.5, priority 1).** Runs only if a drafts/ timing check shows at least 0.3 ms/step saved. This is the only open Lvl3 hypothesis with no test yet.

Dropped:
- I058 (denser lookahead): the averaging axis is flat and its expected gain is below noise.
- I063 (no translate in any stage): superseded by the low-res-only version.
